comparator_source.rule: every conjunct uses ONLY these frozen rows; the freshly-scored bridge anchor is validation-only and discarded
comparator_source._irreplaceable: regenerated from caches that no longer exist. NEVER overwrite it.

bridge._amended: **AMENDED 2026-09-10 (Fable + Codex round 8, 2026-09-10, independently reproduced here), pre-observation: the inherited tolerance could not be satisfied by a correct run, and failing it CONSUMES THE ACCESS.**
bridge._why: M9's `max_abs_per_query_delta` was 0.0003. **nDCG@10 is quantised**: with binary relevance and >=10 relevant documents IDCG@10 = 4.543559, so the smallest possible NONZERO per-query change — one swap at the deepest ranks — is **0.002633**, about 9x the tolerance. There is no such thing as a per-query delta of 0.0003. The rule therefore passed only if NOT ONE of ~3,727 queries changed ranking at all, i.e. it was bit-exactness wearing a tolerance's clothing. And bit-exactness is unavailable: `results/perquery.json` was regenerated from fp16 artifact caches, `scripts/validate_perquery.py` records that the Mac caches behind it are GONE, and the final run re-encodes on an A100 in fp32. `results/FINAL_MATRIX.md` documents that exact perturbation class moving 4 of 54 cells at the DATASET MEAN, which is impossible without per-query changes above the quantum. A correct run had a real chance of spending the one irreversible access and producing no verdict. Nobody had ever executed this rule.
hard_fail_on: qid SET inequality on any dataset — a missing, extra or reordered query is a different evaluation, not a numerical difference
dataset-level |mean delta| > 0.003 on any dataset — the repo's own harness standard (`results/FINAL_MATRIX.md`), and comfortably above the fp16/fp32 movement it records
report_never_fail: max |per-query delta| and the count of changed queries, per dataset
the mean delta per dataset, signed
bridge._reported_in_the_paper: the bridge's measured agreement is reported beside the headline as a reproduction caveat, whatever it shows. A bridge that fails its dataset-mean bound is a real signal and still consumes the access; one that merely shows per-query movement is the expected consequence of re-encoding on different hardware and is disclosed, not fatal.
bridge.failure: a HARD_FAIL_ON condition consumes the access and no verdict is produced. Per-query movement alone never fails.
bridge.anchor_row_is_discarded: the freshly-scored anchor is validation-only and is discarded; every conjunct uses the frozen rows.
bridge._m9_verbatim_row_restored: hashes verified: qrels, preprocessing, model revisions, dtype, exact-search code, tie-breaking (from `m9/FINAL_LOCK.md` §Phase 1; the first M10 draft dropped this row although the re-registration is 'verbatim').

sequence.rule: FIXED-SEQUENCE GATEKEEPING in the order C1b -> C1a -> C2a -> C2b, each at the FULL one-sided 0.025, STOPPING AT THE FIRST NON-REJECTION. No Holm, no alpha split: a gatekeeping sequence spends the family alpha once, in a pre-fixed order.
sequence.stop: at the first conjunct that does not reject, every later conjunct is NOT TESTED and is reported as NOT TESTED — never as failed, and never skipped over to reach a later one
sequence._fixed_when: instructions-m10.md §Final run, amendment A3, 2026-09-04 — before any M10 six-set output existed and before the screen ran
sequence._why_this_order: the release conjunct on the headline partition is tested first, so the claim the project is actually making is the one that spends the alpha first. M9's claim-table row 'C1 fail, C2 pass -> aim permitted' is DELETED by this design: an aim conjunct is unreachable if its release conjunct did not reject.

pass_rule: a conjunct rejects only if BOTH the bootstrap bound and the sign-flip test reject at 0.025, inside the sequence. Both, not either.

bootstrap.resample: n_d queries with replacement within each dataset
bootstrap.decision_field_def: np.quantile(draws, 0.025, method='inverted_cdf'), FULL PRECISION — the EMPIRICAL quantile, i.e. the 250th order statistic at B = 10,000
bootstrap._quantile_history: M9 used 0.0125 under Holm-2. M10 uses 0.025 under gatekeeping, which is the whole point of a fixed sequence. The Codex pass of 2026-09-04 found the two quantiles named in different files; 0.025 is operative and is fixed here.
bootstrap.draw_plan: ONE frozen plan per partition, byte-identical across every conjunct that reads that partition, digest serialized
bootstrap._method_note: `inverted_cdf`, never `linear`. NumPy's linear method interpolates toward the next order statistic and returns a weakly HIGHER, more permissive bound, which could flip an irreversible gate in the candidate's favour. This exact defect was caught in M9 by code review before any six-set number existed; it is registered here so it cannot recur.

signflip.signs: independent Rademacher per paired query; every conjunct passes the SAME SEED — a same-seed guarantee, not a materialized shared plan. Sharing is comparability, not a condition of marginal validity.
signflip._alpha_note: `alpha` here and `sequence.alpha_per_conjunct` are the same number by construction: the sign-flip is a conjunct of the same test, at the same level. `decide()` reads the sequence value; this one is documentation and must never diverge.

reserved.trigger: if ANY C-conjunct rejects, then execute, unmodified
reserved._why_any: so an aim claim never stands without its descriptive reserved rows (Opus, §Final run change 1). M9's trigger was `if C1 passes`. **Note, (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH): under fixed-sequence gatekeeping 'ANY conjunct rejects' is EQUIVALENT to 'C1b rejects', because C1b is first and nothing later is tested unless it rejected.** The wording is kept as 'any' because it is robust to a future re-ordering, but no reader should think it is a weaker condition than it is.
reserved.leave_one_out: remaining weights renormalized to sum to 1
reserved.fever: labelled a DOUBLE-CONTAMINATED sensitivity row (stella discloses FEVER; it is also a reserved set), zero alpha, never gate-relevant
reserved._one_access: the reserved four carry ONE confirmatory access, unspent through M9.
reserved.crash: per-system atomic outputs; resume at the first incomplete system; scores suppressed until all complete
reserved._six_crash: **Post-tag continuation, named 2026-09-10 (Fable + Codex round 8, 2026-09-10, independently reproduced here).** The first version said 'resume at the first incomplete dataset' while `infra_retry_admissible_iff` allows a retry only when the tag does NOT exist, `recover_path` never re-reads the six, and the mandate re-registers FINAL_LOCK's 'any failure at or after step 3 consumes the access, no rerun under any flag'. So the rule I added had no admissible state — another half-applied correction. **The mode, distinct from pre-tag infra retry and from post-completion `--recover`:** POST-TAG CONTINUATION is admissible iff ALL of — the `m10-six-spent` tag EXISTS on origin; the persisted per-dataset scores are INCOMPLETE; `HEAD` equals the FINAL-RUN-BEGIN commit; and the live registry sha256 equals the one persisted with the scores. It opens ONLY the datasets with no persisted scores, appends them, and stops. It may not re-open a dataset already persisted, may not re-score one, and may not run more than once per incomplete dataset. **This AMENDS the mandate's 'no rerun under any flag' for M10, deliberately and pre-observation** — without it a crash between the tag push and the last dataset's write loses the access outright, which is a worse outcome than a bounded, authenticated continuation.

executor_contract: call `evidence_for` for every conjunct and pass NOTHING else to `decide()`. The items below are properties `evidence_for` already guarantees, restated so the executor cannot re-implement them by hand: they are not instructions to compose a plan yourself (reworded 2026-09-10 — they read as such and contradicted `durability_requirement`).

ONE alignment and ONE draw plan per partition, shared by that partition's two conjuncts. `decide()` verifies this from the evidence: the `draw_plan_sha256` and `qid_sha256` of a partition's conjuncts must be equal, which checks the shared plan and qid identity together.
the bootstrap and the sign-flip computed from the same validated `align_partition` output.

score all four conjuncts in ONE transaction regardless of where the sequence stops — the access is spent either way, and the untested conjuncts' descriptive numbers cost nothing. `decide()` tolerates absent evidence after the stop so a crash mid-scoring is still recoverable, but the executor supplies all four.

**`--recover` compares the PERSISTED run-time `registry_sha256` against the live registry and REFUSES on drift.** That comparison cannot live in `decide()` — re-deriving evidence would stamp the new hash and the check would pass trivially (Fable, 2026-09-10). It is an explicit, tested step of the recover path.
implementation.durability_requirement: **The persisted record is the RAW PER-QUERY SCORES, and `--recover` re-runs `evidence_for` on them.** `decide()` is fed nothing but derived evidence in production. This is Fable's finding 4 (2026-09-10) and it is the only structural answer: `decide()` cannot distinguish `evidence_for` output from a hand-edit of a persisted evidence dict — it was demonstrated that editing two numbers in the JSON turned a true negative into REJECTED with every guard passing, because the digests are presence-only (nothing can recompute them without the scores) and `comparator_source_sha256` is stamped from the registry by `evidence_for`, making the guard's check of it a tautology. Persisting the scores instead removes the forgeable surface rather than guarding it. The scores must be written ATOMICALLY BEFORE `decide()` runs, because the access is spent when the `m10-six-spent` tag is pushed and a malformed record would otherwise consume it and leave no recoverable decision. `--recover` re-derives with NO protected re-read, and that path is tested before the run. Evidence also carries `registry_sha256` so recover can detect registry drift between the run and the recovery. **Four specifics the first version of this text left out (Fable, 2026-09-10), each of which would otherwise be an executor assumption:** (i) **qids are persisted as STRINGS** — a JSON round-trip stringifies keys and re-sorts them lexicographically, and executing that with int qids produced a DIFFERENT bound (0.018701 vs 0.019165) and different digests; BEIR qids are strings, so the record must preserve them as such and `evidence_for` must be re-run on the same key types. (ii) **the run-time `registry_sha256` is persisted WITH the scores** — it is stamped fresh on every `evidence_for` call, so a scores-only record has nothing to compare against and `--recover` could not detect registry drift. (iii) **`access_state_machine` gains an explicit 'persist raw scores atomically' step between 'open six / bridge / score' and 'decisions + digest pushed'.** (iv) **the six get a crash rule**, as the reserved batch already has: a crash between the tag push and the scores write loses the access, so the scores are written per-dataset atomically and the run resumes at the first incomplete dataset. The `--recover` path is tested before the run, and 'it is tested' is itself a deliverable, not an assurance.
executor_deliverables: verify the ACTUAL comparator file's sha256 before scoring — `evidence_for` only stamps the registered value, so the real check cannot live there
bind loaded score rows to checkpoint and system identity, so correctly-named but swapped rows cannot pass
compare every scored qid set against the expected frozen query set: pytrec_eval silently OMITS a run qid that has no qrel

M7's preflight standard (`m7src/final_run.py`:449-483) — both comparators' rows on all six checked for length, duplicates and qid-set equality with the frozen payloads — not merely `final9.preflight`'s sha check
persist string qids and the run-time registry hash with the scores

guard each `evidence_for` call independently: a raise on a conjunct the sequence never reached is recorded and omitted, not fatal

access_state_machine: m10-six-spent tag PUSHED (before any protected read)

**persist the RAW PER-QUERY SCORES atomically, per dataset, with the run-time registry_sha256** — before `decide()` runs, because the access is already spent and a malformed record would otherwise consume it and leave no recoverable decision
decide() on evidence derived by `evidence_for` from those persisted scores
infra_retry_admissible_iff: PRE-TAG only: the `m10-six-spent` tag does not exist on origin. Once it exists, the only admissible re-entries are POST-TAG CONTINUATION (`reserved._six_crash`, incomplete scores only) and `--recover` (decisions only, never re-reading the six). Three modes, disjoint by the tag's existence and by whether the scores are complete.
recover_path: --recover recomputes decisions from results/m10_final_run.json and NEVER re-reads the six
_forbidden_note: in the report's description of any final-run outcome. A screen contrast 'resolves'; a final-run conjunct REJECTS or does not. Keeping the vocabularies apart is what stops a screen verdict being read as a release claim.

Each is emitted ONLY if its own conjunct REJECTED, and never if that conjunct was NOT_TESTED.

_origin_note: the spend receipt's external witness. Pinned so repointing `origin` cannot manufacture an 'unspent' verdict. Derived from `git remote get-url origin`, never hand-written.
_guard: `final10.assert_evidence_matches_registry` checks quantile, quantile_method, B, k_datasets, the scored dataset set and the sign-flip p-value AT the decision boundary. M9 had `final_stats._assert_matches_registry`; the first draft of M10 removed that protection and replaced it with nothing, and both reviewers demonstrated evidence tagged quantile=0.0125, method='linear', B=9 and even signflip_p=-1 being accepted as REJECTED (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH).
forbidden_words_scope: The banned words apply to the REPORT'S CHARACTERISATION OF A FINAL-RUN OUTCOME — never to the screen, whose registered vocabulary is exactly 'resolved' / 'did not resolve' / 'unresolved' (`instructions-m10.md` claim table). Flagged (Codex + Fable adversarial review of the lock, 2026-09-09; both returned DO NOT PUSH) as a contradiction; it is a scoping question, not a conflict: a SCREEN contrast resolves or does not, a FINAL-RUN conjunct rejects or does not, and the report must not swap the two vocabularies.
